findings.bible: Presence, privileges, and profile: GamerPresence supplies all 60 XNA display strings and formats parameterized modes; the publication hook is empty (ledger WP15-ch49-030 corrected the formatting claim).
findings.target: modules/gamer-services/src/Xna/GamerPresence.cpp::presenceModeStrings_ is an alphabetically sorted 60-entry table ("Arcade Mode", "At Menu", "Battling Boss", ...), and setPresenceModeProperty indexes it with static_cast<size_t>(mode); modules/gamer-services/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/GamerServices/GamerPresenceMode.hpp declares the enum in XNA order (None, SinglePlayer, Multiplayer, ...). So None -> "Arcade Mode", SinglePlayer -> "At Menu", Winning (ordinal 28) -> the empty entry. The hook is only called when the selected string differs from the previous one, and setPresenceValueProperty re-passes the previous string without selecting a template. Published Known Issue CNA-BUG-173 records the same mismapping.
findings.site_now: deep-dives/services/gamer-services-contract.html#presence: says setting PresenceMode/PresenceValue "selects a template" and that "the publication hook is where one would attach"; it never says the selected template is wrong, and the page carries no link to CNA-BUG-173 although that entry lists this page as its deep dive. The ledger verification of WP15-ch49-030 read the same functions but did not compare the table order with the enum.

fix.old_html: Setting PresenceMode or PresenceValue stores the value, selects a template, and passes the template to SetPresenceModeStringEXT, whose body is empty. Nothing substitutes PresenceValue into {0}, and the selected string is private: no getter exposes it. The observable contract is therefore just the two stored properties. There is no service to publish presence to, and the publication hook is where one would attach.
fix.html: Setting PresenceMode stores the mode, indexes the table with the enum's ordinal and passes the resulting string to SetPresenceModeStringEXT (only when it differs from the previously selected one); setting PresenceValue stores the value and passes the current string again. The hook's body is empty. Nothing substitutes PresenceValue into {0}, and the selected string is private: no getter exposes it. The lookup is also wrong for almost every mode: the table is sorted alphabetically while GamerPresenceMode follows XNA's declaration order, so None selects "Arcade Mode", SinglePlayer selects "At Menu" and Winning selects the empty entry (CNA-BUG-173; read from the source, not executed). Nothing can observe that today, so the observable contract is just the two stored properties. There is no service to publish presence to, and a publisher attached to the hook would receive the wrong text until the table is fixed.

findings.bible: Guide overlays and stubs: "Escape cancels the operation"; "The test corpus covers pending state, callback identity, Enter and Escape, prompt fields, password display, and competing requests."

The message-box real click path, by contrast, is driven through a CannedMousePlatform (TheClickThatAnswersAMessageBoxDoesNotAlsoReachTheGame).
findings.site_now: deep-dives/services/gamer-services-contract.html#guide: "The service tests cover ... Enter and Escape ... driven through simulation helpers" - true only for the simulated cancel; the real Escape edge in the render hook (the only path that cancels in a running game) is unexercised, and the same page says Escape cancels only through that hook.

findings.bible: Local identities and object lifetime (not stated in the Bible): the gamer collections are the way applications find their local identities; raised because the audit rule is that XNA 4.0 wins.
findings.target: modules/gamer-services/src/Xna/SignedInGamerCollection.cpp::operator[](PlayerIndex) casts the index to int and returns collection_[id] (nullptr when id >= size), i.e. by position. XNA 4.0 (decompiled SignedInGamerCollection.this[PlayerIndex]) loops over the gamers and returns the one whose PlayerIndex equals the argument, else null. GamerServicesCollectionsTests.cpp (lines around the PlayerIndex lookups) only builds collections in PlayerIndex order (One, Two, Three), so the difference is unpinned.
findings.site_now: docs/tutorials/123-achievements.html says the PlayerIndex overload "returns nullptr for an empty slot"; development/internals/modules/gamer-services.html#gamer-ownership says it "returns null for an index beyond the collection". Both pages also advise publishing custom gamers with setSignedInGamersProperty, which is exactly when position and PlayerIndex can diverge; neither says the lookup is positional. Not in Known Issues.

fix.old_html: SignedInGamerCollection::operator[](PlayerIndex) returns null for an index beyond the collection rather than throwing.
fix.html: SignedInGamerCollection::operator[](PlayerIndex) returns null for an index beyond the collection rather than throwing, and it indexes by position: it returns the element at that ordinal, where XNA 4.0 returns the gamer whose PlayerIndex matches. The two agree only while the collection is in PlayerIndex order, as the four stubs are; a collection published with Gamer::setSignedInGamersProperty in another order, or without the lower indices, answers differently (the tests only use PlayerIndex-ordered collections).

fix.old_html: there is also an overload taking a PlayerIndex, which returns nullptr for an empty slot.
fix.html: there is also an overload taking a PlayerIndex, which returns nullptr beyond the end of the collection; note that it indexes by position, not by each gamer's own PlayerIndex as XNA does, so it matches XNA only for a collection in PlayerIndex order such as the default four.

findings.target: modules/storage/src/StorageDevice.cpp::StorageDevice::DeleteContainer resolves <root>/<titleName> with ResolveContainedPath and calls remove_all, ignoring the device player; XNA decompile (Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Storage StorageDevice.DeleteContainer -> StorageContainer.DeleteContainer(device, playerIndex, titleName) -> GetDirectoryForContainer(device, displayName, playerIndex)) deletes only <SavedGames>/<title>/<displayName>/Player{N} (or AllPlayers for a device selected without a player), recursively.
findings.site_now: docs/storage.html (Other StorageDevice members table) states CNA removes <root>/<titleName> "(every player folder)"; development/internals/modules/storage.html#deletion says it "ignores the device's player" and that "no FNA behaviour constrains this code". Neither page says XNA 4.0 (the reference that wins) is player-scoped, so a porter of multi-profile save code is not told CNA deletes more.

fix.old_html: Recursively removes <root>/<titleName> (every player folder). Empty, absolute and escaping names throw std::invalid_argument.
fix.html: Recursively removes <root>/<titleName> (every player folder, whichever player the device was selected for). Empty, absolute and escaping names throw std::invalid_argument. XNA 4.0's own DeleteContainer is narrower: it deletes only the device's own Player{N} (or AllPlayers) folder of that title, so CNA's delete also removes the other players' folders (XNA side read from the decompiled reference, CNA side from StorageDevice.cpp; neither executed).

fix.old_html: It also notes that FNA's own DeleteContainer throws NotImplementedException, so no FNA behaviour constrains this code.
fix.html: It also notes that FNA's own DeleteContainer throws NotImplementedException, so no FNA behaviour constrains this code; XNA 4.0 does constrain it: its DeleteContainer resolves the same container path OpenContainer uses, including the device's Player{N} or AllPlayers folder, and deletes only that folder recursively, so a title used by several players loses one player's saves under XNA and all of them here.

findings.bible: Session types and ownership: the create path does not forward maxGamers (limitation note, now stale). Ledger WP15-ch51-008 replaced it with "maxGamers is validated in 2..31 and forwarded".
findings.target: modules/net/src/Xna/NetworkSession.cpp::AddRemoteGamer throws InvalidOperationException("Session is full!") when allGamers_ >= maxGamers_; it is called from modules/net/src/Internal/ENetBackend.cpp::HandleClientHello after AssignWireId/PeerWireIds/WireIdToPeer are filled and after SendTo(peer, ServerWelcome); HandleReceive wraps every handler in catch (const std::exception&) {} . No production code raises NetworkSessionJoinError::SessionFull (grep of modules finds only the enum and the C-API constant). The only test of the limit is NetworkSessionTest.AddRemoteGamerThrowsWhenSessionIsAlreadyAtMaxGamers (unit level); no ENetBackendTests/TwoProcessLoopbackTest case joins a full session.
findings.site_now: deep-dives/services/network-sessions.html#limits: "forwarded to the session and enforced when remote gamers are added (Session is full!)" - true of AddRemoteGamer in isolation, but presented as if a full session refuses joiners. By source reading the host has already welcomed the client and the swallowed exception leaves it half-admitted (in the client's view joined; not in the host's gamer views; no broadcast to the other peers). No Known Issue covers this; it looks like an undocumented defect that merits an entry.

fix.old_html: The requested maxGamers is forwarded to the session and enforced when remote gamers are added (“Session is full!”); a session created with 8 reports 8.
fix.html: The requested maxGamers is forwarded to the session, so a session created with 8 reports 8, and AddRemoteGamer refuses a gamer beyond it with InvalidOperationException (“Session is full!”). Over the wire that refusal is weak: when the host handles a ClientHello it has already sent the joining client its ServerWelcome and registered its wire ids before AddRemoteGamer throws, and the receive path's catch-all drops the exception, so a join beyond the limit is not turned away with NetworkSessionJoinError::SessionFull (that value is never raised at this snapshot) and no test joins a full SystemLink session (read from the source; not executed).

findings.bible: Lifetime hardening: "asynchronous callbacks were stored but not invoked, including reentrant replacement" (FIXED BUG WP15-ch51-040, ledger: confirmed - InvokeActiveActionCallback runs the callback once after activeAction_ is installed and returns the captured action).
findings.target: modules/net/src/Xna/NetworkSession.cpp::InvokeActiveActionCallback copies activeAction_ into a local, calls action->Callback(*action) (Callback is a const std::function member of the action) and returns the local; EndCreate/EndFind/EndJoin do delete activeAction_ (Task 3.2). So a callback that calls End* (the pattern pinned by NetworkSessionTest.BeginCreateCallbackCanReentrantlyCallEndCreate, described there as "the most common real APM usage") deletes the action and the std::function currently executing, and Begin* then returns the freed pointer. That test discards Begin*'s return value and its lambda writes a captured reference after EndCreate returns; BeginCreateInvokesCallbackExactlyOnceWithCorrectIdentity only covers the non-reentrant identity case. The original defect (callback never invoked) is indeed fixed, so this is a residual hazard of the fix, not a restore.
findings.site_now: deep-dives/services/network-sessions.html#hardening: "Begin* returns the action it created even if the callback already called End*"; development/internals/modules/net.html#create says the same ("still returns the action it made"). Both present the returned pointer as safe; in the re-entrant case it is dangling. The gamer-services internals page uses the same wording, which is correct there because those End* methods do not delete the action.

fix.old_html: the callback now runs once, after the action is installed, and Begin* returns the action it created even if the callback already called End*.
fix.html: the callback now runs once, after the action is installed, and Begin* returns the action it created rather than a stale null. For a session Begin*/End* pair that pointer is not safe to use in one case: a callback that calls the matching End* from inside itself makes End* delete the action, and with it the std::function that is running the callback, so the pointer Begin* then returns is already freed and the callback must not touch its captures after End* returns; no test checks either point (source reading, not executed).

fix.old_html: so a re-entrant callback sees consistent state and the Begin* still returns the action it made.
fix.html: so a re-entrant callback sees consistent state and the Begin* returns the pointer it made, although that pointer is already freed if the callback called the matching End* (End* deletes the action, including the std::function that is running the callback, and the re-entrant test ignores the return value).

findings.target: sharp-runtime@41b918c9 modules/core/include/System/detail/Utf8Scalar.hpp: TryDecodeUtf8Scalar sets length = 1 on a structurally ill-formed sequence but length = the sequence's own length for a structurally valid non-scalar ("length = len; // structurally valid, but not a scalar"); the header explains the two forms (reporting for Rune, substituting DecodeUtf8Scalar always 1). modules/text/src/System/Text/UTF8Encoding.cpp::wellFormedUtf8Length returns len on success and 0 otherwise, and GetString/GetBytes then do ++i. modules/text/tests/System/Text/Utf8SharedScalarDecodeTests.cpp pins both behaviours (RuneConsumesTheWholeSequenceForANonScalarButOneByteForABreak; AnEncodingSubstitutesOneReplacementPerByteForBothKinds).
findings.site_now: deep-dives/sharp-runtime/streams-text-and-tasks.html#utf8: "On any failure the function reports a length of one, so the caller advances exactly one byte" - wrong for the surrogate and above-U+10FFFF cases of the very function it names, and it omits the two-form design the header documents; a maintainer reusing TryDecodeUtf8Scalar in another encoding would advance by the sequence length and emit one replacement per sequence instead of per byte. The observable UTF8Encoding behaviour stated on the page is correct.

fix.old_html: On any failure the function reports a length of one, so the caller advances exactly one byte.
fix.html: TryDecodeUtf8Scalar is the reporting form: for a structurally ill-formed sequence (bad lead or continuation byte, truncation, overlong) it reports a length of one, but for a structurally valid encoding of a non-scalar (a surrogate, or a value above U+10FFFF) it reports the sequence's own length, so that Rune::TryGetRuneAt can skip it whole (RuneConsumesTheWholeSequenceForANonScalarButOneByteForABreak). Encodings use the substituting form, DecodeUtf8Scalar, which always advances one byte and yields U+FFFD, and wellFormedUtf8Length() returns zero for every failure, after which UTF8Encoding itself advances one byte, so replacement stays per byte for every ill-formed case, a directly encoded surrogate included.

findings.target: CNA 009d40f5: nine exception headers declare the protected (SerializationInfo&, StreamingContext&) constructor (GuideAlreadyVisibleException, GamerPrivilegeException, GameUpdateRequiredException, GamerServicesNotAvailableException, NetworkNotAvailableException, NetworkException, NetworkSessionJoinException, StorageDeviceNotConnectedException, ContentLoadException; CNA/Internal/ExceptionSerialization.hpp is a helper, the tenth file). Only NetworkException, NetworkSessionJoinException, StorageDeviceNotConnectedException and ContentLoadException read the store (ReadMessage/ReadInnerException) and declare GetObjectData. In gamer-services/src/Xna the ctors of GuideAlreadyVisibleException, GamerPrivilegeException, GameUpdateRequiredException, GamerServicesNotAvailableException and NetworkNotAvailableException take info/context as unnamed parameters and default-construct the base (NetworkNotAvailableException builds a fixed type-name message), so a round trip loses the message. They work because ... each CNA exception writes and restores its own base state" - counts the helper header as a tenth exception header, attributes GetObjectData to all, and says they all work. fix.old_html: CNA builds on this directly. Its XNA code throws the .NET-shaped types (System::ArgumentOutOfRangeException, System::ObjectDisposedException), and ten of its exception headers, among them ContentLoadException.hpp, NetworkSessionJoinException and StorageDeviceNotConnectedException, declare XNA's documented protected (SerializationInfo, StreamingContext) constructor and GetObjectData. They work because sharp-runtime's SerializationInfo became a real name-to-value store on 2026-09-20 (b36d6503); since System::Exception itself still has no serialization constructor, each CNA exception writes and restores its own base state through ExceptionSerialization.hpp.
fix.html: CNA builds on this directly. Its XNA code throws the .NET-shaped types (System::ArgumentOutOfRangeException, System::ObjectDisposedException), and nine of its exception headers declare XNA's documented protected (SerializationInfo, StreamingContext) constructor, among them ContentLoadException.hpp, NetworkSessionJoinException and StorageDeviceNotConnectedException. Only four of the nine (ContentLoadException, NetworkException with its subclass NetworkSessionJoinException, and StorageDeviceNotConnectedException) write and restore anything: sharp-runtime's SerializationInfo became a real name-to-value store on 2026-09-20 (b36d6503), and since System::Exception itself still has no serialization constructor, each of those declares GetObjectData and writes and restores its own message and inner exception through ExceptionSerialization.hpp. The round trip is in-process: an inner exception travels as a std::exception_ptr and no bytes are written anywhere. The other five (GuideAlreadyVisibleException, GamerPrivilegeException, GameUpdateRequiredException, GamerServicesNotAvailableException and NetworkNotAvailableException) declare the constructor for signature compatibility and ignore its arguments, so restoring one from a store yields a default message (read from the source; not executed).
